title: Calibration Technologists and Technicians
description: Execute or adapt procedures and techniques for calibrating measurement devices, by applying knowledge of measurement science, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and electronics, sometimes under the direction of engineering staff. Determine measurement standard suitability for calibrating measurement devices. May perform preventive maintenance on equipment. May perform corrective actions to address identified calibration problems.

tasks.text: Calibrate devices by comparing measurements of pressure, temperature, humidity, or other environmental conditions to known standards.
Disassemble and reassemble equipment for inspection.
Operate metalworking machines to fabricate housings, jigs, fittings, or fixtures.
Conduct calibration tests to determine performance or reliability of mechanical, structural, or electromechanical equipment.
Verify part dimensions or clearances using precision measuring instruments to ensure conformance to specifications.
Visually inspect equipment to detect surface defects.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Analyze test data to identify defects or determine calibration requirements.
Attend conferences, workshops, or other training sessions to learn about new tools or methods.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Develop new calibration methods or techniques based on measurement science, analyses, or calibration requirements.
Draw plans for developing jigs, fixtures, instruments, or other devices.
Maintain or repair measurement devices or equipment used for calibration testing.
Order replacement parts for malfunctioning equipment.
Plan sequences of calibration tests according to equipment specifications and scientific principles.
Read blueprints, schematics, diagrams, or technical orders.
Write and submit reports about the results of calibration tests.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: MathWorks Simulink, Minitab, The MathWorks MATLAB.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD, Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D, Bentley MicroStation, Dassault Systemes SolidWorks.
